evidence._control: The reworked configuration re-rendered from a different invocation is byte-identical to the sweep cell it was chosen from, so the render is reproducible and the frame is not stale. K=1 writes no tonemap-exposure key and is byte-identical to the pre-4t build, which is the negative control the self-test runs.

what_is_good: The pinned top of the ladder is gone: the deck strip sat at 0.94 linear at every gain over a x5.7 exposure range and is now 0.4987, measured, on the room's own gate shot.
No clipped pixels at any of the three distances, from 2.12% at the longest sightline.
The emissive and lit populations are now orthogonal knobs, which is the first shape control in tools/export_scene.py; every previous knob moved level only.
The rejected ambient row is recorded with its measurements rather than deleted, so the next session does not re-derive 0.094 and spend the same renders.

findings.text: The floor pools are still featureless white at half distance. They are CAST light, not emission, so the compensated pair holds them invariant by construction and cannot reach them. The room is also a single warm hue throughout with no colour separation between key and fill. Falls apart at half distance on the pools; holds on the wall, the arches and the deck tiling, which the before frame did not.

Level goes x1.05 -> x0.77 against a x1.05-1.75 window: the room leaves the window by its bottom edge, because 23% of the frame's median was the emissive population. Not recoverable here -- at K=4 and exposure 0.73 the median returns to x0.91 and p5 returns to x1.50, exactly where it started. Level and shadow are one degree of freedom until the fittings can carry the level without also filling.

K is solved against one reference frame (more zocalo.png) measured by one code path. No second source that could not have copied the first. Two of OUR cameras agreeing (10.86 and 11.12) is not a cross-check, it is the same scene twice.

Nothing measures the cost of this change. It adds no geometry, no lights and no draw calls -- it rescales existing light energies and one Environment float -- but 'it should be free' is not a measurement and there is no gate that would notice if it were not.

Two sweeps this session were discarded: five --fixture-energy cells came back with two frames sharing an md5 with a third run's output, because station/generated/scene/<shot>/ is rewritten by every render. Re-run strictly sequentially all cells differed. Nothing in the pipeline asserts that a PNG was rendered from the scene.json the same invocation wrote; the tell is an md5 collision between runs that differ in a flag, and it is found by looking rather than by a gate.

what_is_good: The room has a KEY. The concourse's principal fitting was measured in layer 4, quoted in materials.py, and cast no light in any frame this project has ever taken; it now casts, from the position its own record specifies, and the position is derived from the geometry rather than tabulated.

The room has two registers. Every photon it cast before was orange (rib lamp 1.000/0.398/0.233 at energy_rel 0.30 and stall festoon 1.000/0.492/0.420 at 0.19) over a grey ambient. The deck is now lit at 7740 K against a warm vault, which is the warm/cool split the reference has and this file's own doctrine calls 'most of what a Babylon 5 corridor looks like'.

The chair and stool legs cast into the deck. The critic's finding was that they stood in a pool and cast nothing; the layer-4 record says the same thing from the other side, as a measurement -- 'Chair legs cast two to three distinct shadows each, so the deck's brightness is from OVERHEAD sources and not from an emissive floor plate.'
The ambient is the reference's own measured 0.094 instead of the residential corridor's 0.300, closing the defect AMBIENT_SOLVED's header describes and eleven other bespoke places still have.
The units trap that cost this round a set of frames is written above the entry that caused it, not in a commit message: --fixture-energy defaults to 3.0 and the table entry is half of a product.

findings.where: tools/export_scene.py FIXTURE_LIGHTING, the Zocalo rig as a whole
findings.text: The room is now too UNIFORMLY lit, which is the opposite of round 1's defect and still C3. Whole-frame p99/median is 3.98 on the far camera against the reference's 10.87; p5 is x1.94 against a x1.29 band and crushed is 1.86% against the reference's 48.51%. The show's Zocalo is a dark room with bright pools and ours is an evenly lit hall -- 48 keys at a 50 deg cone from 7.2 m plus 96 stall lamps and 60 rib lamps leave nowhere dark. Part of the gap is framing rather than light (the reference is a close shot with dark figures filling the foreground and ours is an empty hall), and that part is not recoverable by any knob in this file; the rest is real. Falls apart at half distance on the far bulkhead, which is one flat value with drawn-on seams carrying two soft key spills and nothing else.

The centreline strip is still the brightest object in every frame and still reads as a painted ribbon: 149,157,169 sRGB against a deck at 117-138, uniform along its whole 64.8 m with no falloff, no interruption and no fitting. K took it from 247 to 149 and cannot take it further without costing the level. Its layer-4 record classes it `emissive_only` at energy_rel 0.25, so a light is not the answer -- what it needs is either a lower emission_energy in materials.py (it shares zoc_deck_light with the pools at 3.5, and the record separates them at 1.00 and 0.25) or interruption in the geometry. Neither file is this item's.

The map-face budget is a geometric count, not a timing. An omni is charged 6 and a spot 1 because a cube map has six faces, which is right if spot and cube-face maps are allocated at the same resolution and wrong if they are not, and nothing in this container can measure a shadow map's cost -- docs/AAA-STANDARD.md says so under 'Shader cost'. What IS measured: the Zocalo's caster count goes 2 -> 12 at an unchanged face budget, and the far camera's render reports 7 casters against 12 on the two near ones, so the ration is spending what it is given. The light count itself is unchanged at 240 and no geometry was added.

Nothing asserts that materials.light_market_pool and FIXTURE_LIGHTING['zoc_downlight'] cannot both cast. They are the same fitting described in two files; today only one of them can reach a frame because station/zocalo.py emits no `light_market_pool` group, and the moment it does the room gets its key twice. That is the failure mode ROBUSTNESS 5 names -- 'nothing the module emits can be emitted twice into one scene without an assertion catching it'.

'The floor light pools are clipped pure-white ellipses with a hard edge, no penumbra, no bounce tint, and -- the giveaway -- no occlusion.' Measured rather than argued: the pools were never at 255 (0.000% of either frame is >= 235 in all channels; they peak at 201 sRGB before and 169 after), so the pure-white reading was wrong about the pixels and right about the look. What has changed is the three things behind it. OCCLUSION: 12 casters where there were 2, and the stool legs darken the deck under every near table -- crop out/after/far.png at (820,400)-(1280,660) against the same box in out/before/far.png. EDGE: |dI/dx| p99.9 across the deck falls 95 -> 73, 102 -> 78, 67 -> 50. SOURCE: the pools now have one, 7.2 m overhead at the soffit, at the position their own layer-4 record specifies.

findings.where: the round-1 critic's separate note on colour
findings.text: 'Nothing in these frames is a saturated accent ... Until the rig emits coloured practicals, this room will keep scoring 3 no matter what the global exposure is.' Half answered. The rig now emits a second register -- a 7740 K cool key over the deck against the 2990 K vault -- which is what the reference's own measurement says the room is. It does NOT emit the reference's saturated practicals, and the reason is recorded rather than deferred: layer 4 classes zoc_neon_face, zoc_screen and zoc_deck_strip `emissive_only`, i.e. it measured them and found they light nothing, and their halo in the reference dies within 0.4 of the sign's own height. Making them cast would be inventing throw against a measurement. The saturation has to come from materials.py's emission and from geometry that is missing -- the reference's green-ringed table lamps have no group in station/zocalo.py at all.
